reason: A margin torn into hair-like segments is fringed (fimbriate). One fringed annotation keeps more of the meaning than lacerate (FLOPO:0991115) plus ciliated as two separate values.
'Inflorescence a compound umbel' names the kind of inflorescence. compound umbel is an EXACT synonym of PO_0030130.

label: depressed obovate
definition: An obovate quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's widest part being above the middle and its width being greater than its length.
reason: A named plane shape in the Systematics Association chart (odp reference 10), not a run between two values. FLOPO:0991103 depressed is a 3-D flattening and does not fit a flat leaflet.
'Laxly/densely flowered' is a quality of the inflorescence towards its flowers: loose (PATO_0001802) or dense (PATO_0001164) towards flower. The flower counts in the same statements go to pattern 03.
The foot is the orchid column foot, a part. The quality is length (PATO_0000122) with a measured value.
Negates coherent, i.e. like parts (pappus bristles, calyx lobes) that do not stick together. 'At apex' and 'bases' name regions of the bearer.

target: new: colour of a surface marking
reason: Two values in one phrase: banded (PATO_0001946, EXACT synonym striped) and purple (PATO_0000951), where purple is the colour of the stripes, not of the whole part. A pattern should link the colour to the marking instead of making one term per colour.
Supra-axillary inflorescences arise above the axil, displaced up the internode, so they are a kind of extra-axillary. With 11 statements, a rule to the existing term is better than a new child class.

An OCR split of 'semi-drop-shaped', which should be repaired at transcription. Even repaired, a half teardrop (cf. PATO_0002240 teardrop-shaped) in a few bulbil statements is too rare and vague for a term.
A moss costa structure, not a quality. 'Lacking an adaxial pad' is an absence (pattern 15), but PO has no class for the pad, so neither an absence rule nor a bearer rule can be written.
The source words are 'obovales-oblancéolées', a run between obovate (PATO_0001936) and oblanceolate (PATO_0002330). The word's label is a mistranslation.
A likeness to another structure ('en forme d'androgynophore'), with no shape that can be defined. It is rare and its meaning depends on the context.
'Pluri-nerved' means many veins: an indefinite count of vein (nerved → vein in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv).
A pubescence of appressed stiff hairs is strigose. 'Pubescent' adds nothing that strigose does not already say.
Same as 'pluriveined': an indefinite count of vein.

label: anterior (sensu botany)
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being located on the side of a flower or floral whorl away from the axis that bears it, towards the subtending bract.
reason: The floral-diagram position of a member of a series. It would be used with pattern 18 beside FLOPO:0991381 median and FLOPO:0991380 lateral (sensu botany). PATO_0001632 'anterior to' is relational and based on an animal body axis.
Divided into hair-like segments, i.e. fringed. Same reading as 'ciliate-lacerate'.
Strigillose is a spelling of strigulose. 'Densely' is a degree that stays in the record.
A length measured on the lower region of a part (capsule, pedicel), not a quality word. Some examples (the corolla length) do not mention a lower part at all.
The phrase names a part (testa) together with an existing quality, smooth (PATO_0000701).
'Pedicels/filaments of variable length' means members of a set that differ in size, which is unequal. Heterostyly in the style example is FLOPO:0991137 only when the source says so.
A likeness to a laurel leaf with no fixed shape. Floras use it as an alternative to elliptic ('lauriformes ou elliptiques'), so mapping it to PATO_0000947 elliptic would be doubtful.
The acumen is the drawn-out tip of the leaf apex, and the quality is width (PATO_0000921). Several examples give whole-blade measurements and must not be read as acumen width.

The bearer is leaf base (PO_0020040), 'broadly' is a degree, and 'rounded' is read as obtuse as in the reviewed leaf-base rows. Some union-pair reviews (for crowns, and in one base pair) call obtuse a wrong grounding for 'rounded', so a later review of base shape may change this rule.
A part plus length (PATO_0000122). In the source the lobes are often given in statements about the flower or fruit, which is pattern 12 (part of a qualified whole).
'Attached laterally to the mericarp' is an attachment towards another part, with the place of attachment on the side. Unlike dorsifixed or basifixed, the other part is always named.
Caducous is already grounded to fugacious (falling very early). 'Very' is a degree that stays in the record.
Like parts (sepals, styles) fused together are connate. 'At base' names the region, and 'joined' alone already maps to fused with PATO_0000642.
A part plus length (PATO_0000122). spike is an EXACT synonym of PO_0030117.

The examples mix three unrelated senses: an 'abscission vein', circumscissile shedding of a calyx, and leaf abscission zones present. As a single word it is a process or part, not a quality, and needs its context.
